summary: A small developer script that looks up one user account by email and prints the stored details.
purpose: Lets a developer check whether a specific account exists and see its stored fields.
why: Likely reason: a quick debugging helper. Reason not stated in the code.
how: First it creates a database client. Then it looks up one user whose email matches a value written into the file. It prints the result as formatted text. Last it disconnects from the database.
inputs: A hardcoded email address in the file and the database connection setting.
outputs: Text printed to the terminal: the full user record, or null if no user matches.
risks: The script prints every stored field of the account, which may include personal or health-related data, so the output should not be pasted into shared logs. The target email is written into the source, so it checks only one account.
debug: If nothing prints, check the database connection and that the email is spelled exactly as stored. If an import error appears, the generated client may need to be created first.
